newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission confirms five green rate changes.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission confirms five green rate changes.

text.p: The European Commission on Friday confirmed five changes to green rates, used to conduct cross-frontier trade in farm products, with effect from Saturday.
The new rates reflect devaluations in the formerly strong German mark, Dutch guilder and Austrian schilling, with the Irish punt continuing to revalue.
Sterling, formerly a weak currency, enters a fifth and final confirmation period and could revalue on January 21, wiping out gains to farmers during a long series of devaluations.

The green mark will devalue to 1.94738 per Ecu from 1.94386, the green guilder will devalue to 2.18573 per ecu from 2.18167, the green schilling will devalue to 13.7020 from 13.6782 and the green Belgian franc will devalue to 40.1295 from 40.0486.
The green Irish punt will revalue to 0.778173 per Ecu from 0.812908. --Chris White, Brussels Newsroom ++ 32 2 287 6830
